To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a stochastic point process adaptive filter was used successfully to track the evolution of nonlinear kernels in simulated neural networks.
a stochastic state point-process filter can be used to reconstruct the nonlinear kernels in a nonlinear dynamical system from spike input and spike ouput information alone.
the proposed method is capable of tracking the temporal evolution of neural systems in real time, and that it can be used for the analysis of the functional properties of neural systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of methods for the analysis of neural systems.
the development of a new method for modeling neural population dynamics.
the development of a new approach to model and analyze the dynamics of neural systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the method proposed in this thesis provides an accurate, robust and computationally feasible approach to the nonstationary nonlinear system identification problem.
the method proposed here can be used to estimate the feedforward and the feedback kernels of the system under investigation.
a new method has been developed for tracking the time-dependent changes of nonlinear neural system dynamics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we can track the functional properties of a system by observing the input-output spike train data of the system.
we have developed a new method to model neural population dynamics and to reconstruct the underlying nonlinear feedforward and feedback connectivity of neural populations from spike data.
we developed a new approach to estimate the functional properties of a neural population from spike input and spike response data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Laguerre coefficients can be estimated in a nonstationary setting using a point-process model and can be used to reconstruct the underlying nonlinear dynamics.
a state point-process adaptive model is capable of tracking the evolution of nonlinear dynamical systems with time-varying parameters.
a stochastic state point-process model of neural dynamics can be used to estimate the feedforward and recurrent kernels underlying a population of neurons.
